tools.description: Capture an HTTP(S) page, including localhost dev servers, as a PNG or import it as editable layers. import_element needs a CSS selector. Give the viewport in pixels; additional asset origins need separate permission. embed adds a live website node. Imports need a parent and use one undoable transaction. Unsupported content is reported in notes. Open a document first so network permissions can be recorded.
tools.name: browser

tools.description: Claim a frame before working in it, so other agents cannot change it while you do. The claim lapses after 60 seconds without a change from you, and a person can always edit or stop it. Claim fails when another agent holds the frame; pick another one or wait.

document.description: The document. Defaults to the one opened last.

tools.name: claim_frame

tools.description: Copy layers, with everything inside them, to a page or layer. Copies get new ids, returned in the order of `copies`. One change for the whole batch.

copies.description: What to copy and where each copy goes.

index.description: Where among the parent's children, back to front. Defaults to the top (the end).

parent.description: The page or layer it goes into, by id.

document.description: The document. Defaults to the one opened last.

tools.name: copy_nodes

tools.description: Make layers into components: each layer's tree becomes a component definition and the layer becomes its first instance. Returns the component ids in order; use create_instance to place more.

document.description: The document. Defaults to the one opened last.

ids.description: The layers to make into components. Each stays where it is, as the first instance of its component.

tools.name: create_component

tools.description: Place instances of local components, with their props and overrides. Each is sized like its component unless `set` says otherwise. Returns the new ids in order, as one change.

document.description: The document. Defaults to the one opened last.

component.description: The local component, by id (list_components shows them).

index.description: Where among the parent's children, back to front. Defaults to the top (the end).

parent.description: The page or layer it goes into, by id.

set.description:
Instance properties in the file format: `name`, `position`, `width`, `props` (the component's props by
name), `overrides`. Size and name default to the component's.

tools.name: create_instance

tools.description: Remove layers and everything inside them, as one change. The person can undo it; still, read what you are removing first.

document.description: The document. Defaults to the one opened last.

ids.description: The layers to remove, each with everything inside it.

tools.name: delete_nodes

tools.description: Run a short JavaScript program against the document's `doc` API: loops and variables do in one call what would take many tool calls. The whole script is one change and one undo step; if any call fails, nothing is applied and the error names the line. `validate_only` reports what would change. Limits: 5 seconds, 2,000 calls, 2,000 new layers; no network, files or timers.

code.description:
A JavaScript program using `doc` (read_skill "execute" documents it): doc.page, get, query, insert,
update, copy, replace, move, delete, setVariables, createComponent, makeSlot, instance, findSpace,
layoutProblems, screenshot, export, claim, release. `return` a value to get it back; return
doc.screenshot(id) to see the result.

document.description: The document. Defaults to the one opened last.

validate_only.description: Run it and report what would change, without changing anything.

tools.name: execute

tools.description: Export selected layers to PNG, JPEG, WEBP, SVG, PDF, HTML + CSS or HTML + Tailwind. Returns named files as MIME/base64 data, warnings and, for one PNG or inline HTML output, clipboard MIME data. PDF pages follow selection order; multiple raster images become a ZIP. HTML includes its styles and works offline. No file is written. The caller saves the bundle; agent file writes require permission.

assets.description: Inline HTML assets (default) or return them as additional files in the bundle.

format.description: png, jpeg, webp, svg, pdf, html-css or html-tailwind.

nodes.description: Layer or page ids, in selection order. PDF uses this as page order; multiple rasters return a ZIP.

scaffold.description: Include a complete HTML page (default true).

scale.description: Raster scale: 1, 2 or 3. Vector and code exports retain canvas units.

suffix.description: A filename suffix. Unsafe characters become hyphens; never interpreted as a path.

tools.name: export

tools.description: Write the document's variables as a token file: CSS variables, a Tailwind v4 `@theme` block, or Design Tokens (DTCG) JSON. Returns the file's text and a file name to suggest; write it into the project yourself. Each theme value (such as dark) is written under the selector in `mapping`, which you can change. `warnings` names every token or value that could not be written.

document.description: The document. Defaults to the one opened last.

oneOf.description: CSS custom properties: `:root { --color-primary: #2563EB; }` and a block per theme value.
A Tailwind v4 stylesheet: `@theme { … }` and a block per theme value.

lengths.description:
Name prefixes whose numbers are lengths and so are written with `px`. Replaces the defaults (space, spacing,
radius, size, width, height, gap, border, stroke, blur, container, breakpoint, text, font/size).

mapping.description:
Rows to change in the mapping of theme values to selectors. Only the rows you name change; a value the
document lacks is added to its axis.

items.description: Which selector a theme value is written under.

selector.description:
The CSS selector: `.dark`, `[data-theme="dark"]`. The first value of an axis is its default and is always
written under `:root`.

namespaces.description: Token namespaces written under another name in the file, such as {"space": "spacing"}.

tools.name: export_tokens

tools.description: Fill a layer with a real picture: a file from the repository (`path`), a picture you hold (`data`, base64) or a stock photo found by words (`query`), or a generated image (`prompt`, configured `model`). The picture is stored in the repository next to the document. An image layer gets the new picture; any other shape gets an image fill. A stock photo's author, page and licence are written to the layer's metadata. Reading a file or reaching the stock library asks the person first.

data.description: A picture as base64 (a `data:` URL also works). Needs no permission.

document.description: The document. Defaults to the one opened last.

fit.description: How the picture fills the layer: "fill" (cover, the default), "fit" (contain) or "stretch".

model.description: The image model id. Defaults to the model configured in native image settings.

node.description: The layer to fill: an image layer, or a frame, rectangle, ellipse or other shape.

path.description: A picture file (PNG, JPEG or WEBP) in the repository. Needs the person's permission.

prompt.description: Generate an image using the provider configured in Settings, Assets.

query.description:
Words to find a stock picture with. The picture is downloaded into the repository, so the design never
depends on the stock site. Needs the person's permission to reach it, and a key in Settings, Assets.

result.description: With `query`: which result to use, counting from 0. Defaults to 0, the best match.

tools.name: fill_image

tools.description: List every distinct value a property takes in a scope, with how many nodes have each and a few example ids. Use it to see what a design already uses (font sizes, colours, radii) before adding more, or to find values that should be a variable. Variable references show as {"$var": id}.

document.description: The document. Defaults to the one opened last.

limit.description: The most distinct values to list (default 100, at most 500).

property.description:
The property, in the file's spelling, with dots into nested objects. Lists are looked through, so
`content.size` is every text run's size and `fills.color` is every fill colour. Examples: `cornerRadius`,
`gap`, `content.font`, `stroke.width`.

scope.description: Only look inside this page, component or node.

tools.name: find_properties

tools.description: Find an empty area of the canvas of a given size, clear of every frame already on the page and of every planned frame an agent has reserved. Use it to place a new top-level frame instead of guessing coordinates. Returns the rectangle.

document.description: The document. Defaults to the one opened last.

height.description: The height of the area needed.

near.description: Prefer the free area nearest this point.

page.description: The page to look on. Defaults to the first page.

width.description: The width of the area needed.

tools.name: find_space

tools.description: Report what is open and what the person sees: open documents, the active one, its selection and viewport, which frames are leased (and by which agent; `you` is this client's), the planned frames other agents have reserved (placeholders: leave their areas free), which agents are paused, and the notes for agents and context nodes that apply to the selection (or the page, with no selection). Call it first, and again before starting on a new request.

document.description: The document whose selection, leases and notes to report. Defaults to the active document.

tools.name: get_app_state

tools.description: Read nodes by id, with their children down to `depth`. Use it to look at a frame before changing it. Children past the depth are counted in `childCount`; nodes past `max_nodes` come back as stubs.

depth.description:
How many levels of children to include: 0 is the node alone with a `childCount`, 1 (the default) adds
its children. At most 8.

document.description: The document. Defaults to the one opened last.

ids.description: The ids of the nodes to read. Page ids are not nodes; use query_nodes with `scope` to list a page.

max_nodes.description:
Stop after this many nodes in all (default 300, at most 2000). Nodes past it come back as stubs with
`truncated: true`.

tools.name: get_nodes

tools.description: Describe a frame so you can write its code: its layers with layout, sizing, fills and text; every design token it uses, by name, with its value under each theme; and the components its instances use, with props and definition. Pass `stack` (shadcn, react-native or swiftui) to also get that stack's hints for writing each part. The spec is the design's own words, not code. Use tokens by name instead of copying their values, and use snapshot_layout when you need rendered sizes.

document.description: The document. Defaults to the one opened last.

frame.description: The frame (or any layer) to describe, by id.

stack.description:
The stack you will write the code in: `shadcn`, `react-native` or `swiftui`. Adds that stack's hints on how
to write each part. Without it, the answer lists the stacks there are.

tools.name: get_spec

tools.description: List visual styles, or load one by name: palette, typography, radius and density. Use a recipe when no design system is set; existing document variables and system guidelines take precedence. Loading a style does not edit the document or install fonts.

name.description: A name returned by get_style. Omit to list the available recipes.

tools.name: get_style

tools.description: List the document's variables (colours, numbers, strings, booleans) and its theme axes. Each shows its id, name and type, the value it has under the theme, and every value it can take. Bind a property to a variable with {"$var": id}; prefer a variable over a literal that matches one.

document.description: The document. Defaults to the one opened last.

name.description: Only variables whose name contains this, ignoring case.

theme.description: Theme axis values to resolve under, such as {"Mode": "dark"}. Axes left out take their first value.

tools.name: get_variables

tools.description: Remove an image background using the configured local ONNX model, or trace flat artwork into editable vectors with vtracer. Uses the selected image layer or a shape with one image fill, preserves its id and placement, and commits one undoable attributed transaction. No network or automatic model downloads.
tools.name: image_ops

tools.description: Bring existing content onto the canvas as editable layers: an SVG (shapes become rectangles, ellipses and vectors, text becomes text), a PNG, JPEG or WEBP picture (an image layer, the file stored in the repository), or layers copied from Figma (pass the clipboard HTML as `text`; pictures do not come across). Give a file `path` (needs the person's permission) or the content inline as `data` or `text`. For a full Figma file, give figma (a design URL or key); its token stays in the OS keychain. Returns the new layer ids and notes on what could not be imported. BrowserPort computed DOM snapshots use format html.

data.description: The file as base64 (a `data:` URL also works). Needs no permission.

document.description: The document. Defaults to the one opened last.

figma.description: A Figma design URL or file key. Token stays in SecretStore.

format.description: "svg", "image", "figma" or "html" (a BrowserPort computed DOM snapshot). Detected when absent.

index.description: Where among the parent's children, back to front. Defaults to the top.

name.description: The file's name, which names the layer. Taken from `path` when there is one.

parent.description: The page or layer to import into, by id.

path.description: A file in the repository: an SVG, or a PNG, JPEG or WEBP picture. Needs the person's permission.

text.description: Text content to import: SVG markup, or the HTML a Figma copy puts on the clipboard. Needs no permission.

x.description: Left edge of the imported content inside the parent, for a parent without auto layout.

tools.name: import

tools.description: Read a token file (CSS variables, Tailwind v4 or DTCG JSON) and make the document's variables match it, as one change. A token whose name the document has keeps its variable; new names become new variables; theme values the document lacks are added to its themes. Returns the diff: added, changed, removed. `dry_run` shows it without changing anything. Variables the file lacks are only listed unless `remove_missing` is set. Pass the file's text, not its path.

document.description: The document. Defaults to the one opened last.

dry_run.description: Show the diff and change nothing.

oneOf.description: CSS custom properties: `:root { --color-primary: #2563EB; }` and a block per theme value.
A Tailwind v4 stylesheet: `@theme { … }` and a block per theme value.

lengths.description:
Name prefixes whose numbers are lengths and so are written with `px`. Replaces the defaults (space, spacing,
radius, size, width, height, gap, border, stroke, blur, container, breakpoint, text, font/size).

mapping.description:
Rows to change in the mapping of theme values to selectors. Only the rows you name change; a value the
document lacks is added to its axis.

items.description: Which selector a theme value is written under.

selector.description:
The CSS selector: `.dark`, `[data-theme="dark"]`. The first value of an axis is its default and is always
written under `:root`.

namespaces.description: Token namespaces written under another name in the file, such as {"space": "spacing"}.

remove_missing.description:
Also remove the variables the file lacks. They are listed under `removed` either way; one that is still
used cannot be removed, and then nothing is imported.

text.description: The file's text. Read the file yourself and pass its contents.

tools.name: import_tokens

tools.description: Put an icon from an icon library on the canvas as an editable vector layer. Find the library and name with search_icons. Choose size, weight, fill and a colour (or a colour variable). Returns the new layer's id and what was drawn, including when the library could not give the exact weight or fill asked for.

color.description: The colour as #RRGGBB or #RRGGBBAA. Defaults to black. Prefer color_variable when the design has colours.

color_variable.description: A colour variable's id to colour the icon by, so it follows themes.

document.description: The document. Defaults to the one opened last.

fill.description: The filled variant, in libraries that have one.

index.description: Where among the parent's children, back to front: 0 is the bottom. Defaults to the top.

layer_name.description: The layer's name. Defaults to library and icon name.

library.description: The library, as search_icons lists them: lucide, feather, phosphor, material-symbols-outlined, ...

name.description: The icon's name in that library, exactly as search_icons gives it.

parent.description: The page or layer to add the icon to, by id.

size.description: The width of the icon in pixels, 4 to 1024. Defaults to 24.

weight.description:
100 to 700, where 400 is regular. Outline sets draw it as line width; Phosphor has 100, 300, 400 and 700;
Material Symbols has 400. The nearest weight the library has is used.

x.description: Left edge inside the parent, for a parent without auto layout.

tools.name: insert_icon

tools.description: Add nodes (with their children) to a page or a layer, as JSON or as a compact tag spec. All of them go in as one change, or none do. Returns the new top-level ids in order. A mistake is reported with the index and field of the node to fix.

document.description: The document. Defaults to the one opened last.

index.description: Where among the parent's children, back to front: 0 is the bottom. Defaults to the top (the end).

nodes.description: The nodes, in the file format (see read_skill). `id` and `name` may be left out; children nest.

parent.description: The page or layer to add them to, by id.

spec.description:
The nodes as text instead, in `format`. With "jsx" (the default) a tag is a node's type, attributes are
its properties ("text" or {json}), nested tags are children and text inside <text> is its content:
<frame name="Card" width={320} height="hug" layout="column"><text font="Inter" size={14}>Hi</text></frame>

tools.name: insert_nodes

tools.description: List the document's components: id, name, root node, the props an instance can set, the variants, the slots that accept other components, and how many instances use each. Use a component instead of drawing the same thing again.

document.description: The document. Defaults to the one opened last.

name.description: Only components whose name contains this, ignoring case.

tools.name: list_components

tools.description: List the fonts text can use: the families the engine can draw, the fonts stored in this document, and the families its text already uses. A text run names a family; one that is not listed is drawn with a fallback and looks different from what you asked for.

document.description: The document. Defaults to the one opened last.

tools.name: list_fonts

tools.description: List available skills with paths, descriptions and source groups: built-in, design system, yours. Read only the instructions relevant to the task with read_skill; no document needs to be open.
tools.name: list_skills

tools.description: Mark empty frames inside a component as slots, which each instance fills with its own content. Suggest the components that usually go there. One change for the batch.

document.description: The document. Defaults to the one opened last.

slots.description: The frames to make into slots.

id.description: An empty frame inside a component definition (not its root).

suggested.description: Components suggested for the slot, by id. Advisory: anything can fill it.

tools.name: make_slot

tools.description: Move layers to another parent or page, or to another place among their siblings. A layer cannot move into itself or between a page and a component. One change for the whole batch.

document.description: The document. Defaults to the one opened last.

moves.description: What moves where, in order. An index counts the parent's children after the layer has left its old place.

index.description: Where among the parent's children, back to front. Defaults to the top (the end).

parent.description: The page or layer it goes into, by id.

tools.name: move_nodes

tools.description: Open a .vellum document, or create it with `create: true`. If an editor has the file open, work happens in that editor; otherwise the file is opened without one. Returns the pages. Calls that leave out `document` use the document opened last.

create.description: Make the file when it is not there. An existing file is opened, never replaced.

name.description: The name for a new document. Defaults to the file name.

path.description: The path of the .vellum file, relative to the repo.

tools.name: open_document

tools.description: Find nodes by name, type, text, component or variable use, optionally inside one page or node. Returns short summaries in reading order; use get_nodes for the detail. All filters given must match.

component.description: Only instances of this component, by component id.

document.description: The document. Defaults to the one opened last.

limit.description: The most nodes to list (default 50, at most 500). `total` is the full count.

name.description: Only nodes whose name contains this, ignoring case.

scope.description: Only look inside this page, component or node.

text.description: Only text, notes and prompts whose characters contain this, ignoring case.

variable.description: Only nodes that use this variable, by variable id or exact name.

tools.name: query_nodes

tools.description: Read instructions by a path from list_skills: format.md, execute.md, vellum-doc.d.ts, workflows, design-system guidelines or added SKILL.md folders. Omit path to list available skills. Read execute.md before scripting; read relevant guidelines and notes before designing.

path.description: An exact path returned by list_skills. Omit to list. Built-ins also accept the .md path without its extension.

tools.name: read_skill

tools.description: Let go of a frame you claimed, when you are done with it, so other agents can work there.

document.description: The document. Defaults to the one opened last.

tools.name: release_frame

tools.description: Remove layers and put new ones in exactly their place in the layer order. Use it to swap a layer for a different kind of layer; to change properties use update_nodes. Returns the new ids.

document.description: The document. Defaults to the one opened last.

replacements.description: The layers and what replaces each.

node.description: What goes in its place, in the file format. It may keep the old id.

tools.name: replace_nodes

tools.description: Change every use of one value of a property to another, in a scope, as one change: every #111111 text colour to $color/text, every 16 font size to 18. Use find_properties first to see the values in use. Reports how many layers changed; none is not an error.

document.description: The document. Defaults to the one opened last.

from.description: The value to find. `#abc` matches `#AABBCC`; `$color/text` matches a use of that variable.

property.description:
The property, in the file's spelling, dotted into nested objects; lists are looked through. Examples:
`cornerRadius`, `content.size`, `fills.color`, `stroke.width`.

scope.description: Only inside this page, component or layer.

to.description: What to put instead. `$color/text` binds the variable of that name (or id).

tools.name: replace_properties

tools.description: Tell the person how the work is going: what is done and what comes next, and how many plan items are done. When building an approved plan, name the items you just finished in `items` so they tick off. It changes nothing in the document. Call it between parts of a long piece of work.

done.description: How many items of the plan are done.

items.description: The numbers of the plan items finished since the last report. Their placeholders give way to the frames.

message.description: One or two plain sentences on what is done and what is next. Shown to the person as it is.

total.description: How many items the plan has.

tools.name: report_progress

tools.description: Draw a page or node to a PNG you can look at. It is drawn the way the editor draws it. Use it to check your work; large areas at high scale are refused, so draw one frame at a time.

document.description: The document. Defaults to the one opened last.

node.description: The page or node to draw.

scale.description: Pixels per canvas unit, above 0 and at most 4 (default 1).

tools.name: screenshot

tools.description: Find icons by name or meaning in Lucide, Feather, Phosphor and Material Symbols (and the project's own icons when it has some). Returns library and name for each match, best first, with the libraries and the weights each one draws. Pass the library and name to insert_icon.

library.description: Search one library only (see the list the call returns). Searches all of them when left out.

limit.description: The most icons to return, 1 to 100. Defaults to 20.

query.description:
Words to find, such as "arrow right" or "settings". Every word has to match a part of an icon's name or one of
its tags. Leave it out to list the libraries.

tools.name: search_icons

tools.description: Add, change or remove variables (design tokens), as one change. A variable is matched by id or by name, so sending `color/text` again changes it. Returns the id of each by name; bind one with {"$var": id}.

document.description: The document. Defaults to the one opened last.

remove.description: Variables to remove, by id or name. A variable still in use cannot be removed.

variables.description:
Variables to add or change, in the file format: `{"name": "color/text", "type": "color", "values":
[{"value": "#111111"}, {"value": "#EEEEEE", "when": {"Mode": "dark"}}]}`. One with the `id` or the
`name` of an existing variable replaces it; otherwise it is new.

tools.name: set_variables

tools.description: Show the computed layout of a page or node: each node's parent and bounds in page coordinates, and the layout problems found (text overflow, clipped children, overlapping siblings, nodes outside their frame). With `problems_only`, list just the problems and the nodes they involve. Use it after a change to check the result without drawing it.

document.description: The document. Defaults to the one opened last.

max_nodes.description: The most nodes to list (default 300, at most 2000). Past it, `truncated` is true.

node.description: A page or node id. Defaults to the first page.

problems_only.description:
Only the nodes that have a layout problem, and the problems: text that overflows, children a frame clips,
siblings that overlap, nodes outside their frame.

tools.name: snapshot_layout

tools.description: Set properties of layers: name, size, fills, layout, text content and so on, or null to reset one. All updates apply as one change, or none do; a mistake names the update and property to fix.

document.description: The document. Defaults to the one opened last.

set.description:
The properties to set, in the file's spelling. `null` puts one back to its default. Children are changed
with insert_nodes, move_nodes and delete_nodes.

tools.name: update_nodes
